newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's index of 13 top shares launched by IFC.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's index of 13 top shares launched by IFC.

text.p: Morocco's emerging stock market has been included in the International Finance Corporation (IFC) index, a move expected to attract more foreign investors, the Casablanca-based Upline Securities stockbroker said on Tuesday.
The IFC, the private sector arm of the World bank, has also launched indices for Russia and Egypt.

"The IFC attributed to Morocco's index a weight of 0.4 percent in its global calculation of emerging markets. To be noted this weight is superior to those attributed to Egypt and Jordan which represent respectively 0.1 percent and 0.2 percent," Upline Securities said.
Morocco's bourse has 46 listed stocks but the IFC chose only 13 stocks, including the blue chip and largest private conglomerate ONA Group.
Analyst said the stocks were ranked by market capitalisation and value traded.

"The introduction of Morocco in the IFC index has two impacts...It recognises Morocco's financial reforms including the bourse. Morocco will benefit from its introduction in the IFC database which is consulted by thousands of foreign investors," the stockbroker said.
The Casablanca stock exchange all-share index rose beyond 400 points at the end of August, for the first time, traders said.
In 1993, the government launched an ambitious programme to modernise the bourse by introducing new rules and modern financial instruments aimed at more transparency.
With a continuing privatisation programme, it also targeted individuals' saving and small investors, a stockbroker said.

Nearly a dozen companies, among 45 privatised firms, have since been floated on the stock market. Morocco also plans to sell its stakes in around 70 other enterprises including banks and oil refineries, by end 1998.

The (bourse) market capitalisation reached 70.6 billion dirhams ($8.1 billion) in the first nine months of the year, up from 50 billion dirhams in the same period in 1995, an analyst at Upline Securities said.

The 13 Moroccan stocks in the IFC index are ONA, Banque Commerciale du Maroc, Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, Wafabank, Brasseries du Maroc, Ciments de l'Oriental, Lesieur, Credit Eqdom, Samir refinery, Sonasid steel mill, CTM-LN transportation firm and Centrale Laitiere.
The Casablanca bourse, established in 1929, has 12 stockbrokers and 14 mutual funds.
Upline Securities said the bourse accounts for nearly 15 percent of Morocco's Gross Domestic Product in 1996.
